tasks.short: Direct rehearsals and keep useful corrections separate from live instruction.

steps.what: Retrieve the current routine, music references and earlier rehearsal corrections
Direct rehearsals and demonstrate the intended dance steps and effects
Observe dancers rehearsing and assess timing, expression and movement
Check the intended correction and coach dancers through an adjusted attempt
Write the rehearsal corrections and next rehearsal reminders

tasks.design: Configure a routine-linked note view and rehearsal template in {DOCS}. Reference retrieval and correction writing are separately timed; demonstrations, observation and spoken coaching stay with the choreographer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier corrections are scattered and note headings are repeatedly recreated.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document links and reusable rehearsal headings can reduce navigation and entry.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting movement and choosing an explanation that helps each dancer.
tasks.human_edge: Embodied demonstration and a sensitive response to the group.
tasks.altitude: Keep continuity between rehearsals while protecting live coaching time.

evidence.claim: Native linked notes and templates may reduce rehearsal administration; the proposed benefit is E1 rather than a documented choreography case.

assumptions: Baseline includes existing working correction notes, not a newly imposed attendance or performance report.

The choreographer selects routine identity in s1 and captures corrections in s5; neither an automatic movement transcript nor a structured performance feed is assumed. Missing notes require manual reconstruction.
Native document views and templates are tried first; the ordinary author save stays fully retained within s5 without self-approval.
Dancers are internal production colleagues for these instructions.
unknowns: Whether notes are already linked to routine versions
research_questions: Across three rehearsals, do reusable headings reduce note entry without losing useful movement context?

already_counted.description: Reference selection and correction entry remain human

incremental.description: Maintain the routine index and note layout

approvals.approved_version: The specific routine passage, demonstration and current dancers checked immediately before instruction; changed passage requires a new check.
The exact correction and intended dancer checked against the current attempt before communicating it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R96, gross4 minus1 upkeep =3 net. Low: notes have poor routine identifiers and most headings are bespoke, leaving R99 and1 upkeep, net0. High: linked references work but movement descriptions still require full wording, leaving R97 and1 upkeep, net2. All live rehearsal work is retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe technique, advise dancers and separately record useful follow-up notes.

steps.what: Retrieve relevant existing technique notes for the dancer and routine
Observe dancers standing and moving during practice
Judge which dance techniques need correction and recognise limits of coaching
Check and teach the selected technique advice to the dancer
Write brief technique corrections and follow-up points in existing teaching notes

tasks.design: Use native bookmarks and a short technique-note layout in {DOCS}. The choreographer observes, selects and communicates all advice; software neither diagnoses an injury nor prescribes movement corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating earlier technique notes and repeating routine identifiers add small clerical effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Linked teaching notes and reusable headings can reduce this existing handling.
tasks.still_hard: Individual movement differences and whether a concern exceeds the choreographer's competence.
tasks.human_edge: Attentive observation and safe, understandable demonstration.
tasks.altitude: Improve continuity of technique coaching with less repeated note entry.

evidence.claim: A native note template may reduce repeated clerical entry while physical technique coaching remains human; this is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Existing brief teaching notes are counted separately; no new clinical record is assumed.
The choreographer identifies the routine in s1 and supplies technique observations and follow-up text in s2-s5. Missing history is checked manually, not inferred by a model.
The native note layout is sufficient. Author saves remain fully retained with no approval gate.
Advice is given to production colleagues; confidential health details are not required for the proposed template.
unknowns: Whether any existing teaching notes are recorded
Actual access rules for individual notes
research_questions: Does a short note layout save entry time without encouraging unnecessary health-data collection?

already_counted.description: Full observation, judgement and direct coaching

incremental.description: Keep note headings and links current

approvals.approved_version: The specific advice, demonstration and intended dancer checked immediately before delivery; changed movement or feedback requires a fresh judgement.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B100 R97 gives3 gross minus1 upkeep =2 net. Low: individual notes lack routine metadata and corrections are all bespoke, leaving R99 and1 upkeep, net0. High: a reusable routine heading saves entry but not individual wording, leaving R98 and1 upkeep, net1. Observation, judgement and communication remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare teaching materials and teach rhythm and interpretive movement personally.

steps.what: Find suitable rhythm examples and existing interpretive movement teaching materials
Write the lesson sequence and adapt exercises for the performers
Check and teach rhythm and interpretive movement through demonstration and feedback
Record lesson adjustments and useful follow-up exercises

tasks.design: Configure tagged example folders and reusable lesson and follow-up layouts in {DOCS}. Selection, adaptation and live teaching remain human; preparing the lesson and recording its outcomes occur in separate lifecycle steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Examples are hard to locate and recurring lesson structures are rebuilt.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tags and lesson templates can reuse structure without generating artistic decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting rhythm and adapting a demonstration to the learners.

ambition.what: Use any verified preparation capacity for an additional introductory group.

tasks.altitude: Build a reusable teaching library while keeping individual instruction personal.

evidence.claim: Tagged example libraries and lesson templates may reduce preparation handling; no choreography teaching time result is supplied by the digest.

assumptions: Preparation and existing follow-up notes belong to this teaching task; rehearsal corrections belong to the separate rehearsal task.

The choreographer supplies teaching objective and experience level in s1-s2 and records outcomes in s4. Missing example metadata is resolved manually; no structured learner assessment feed is assumed.
Native folders and templates precede custom software. Ordinary saves retain their small effort without author self-approval.
The additional group is optional demand, not included in baseline savings.
unknowns: How much existing material can be reused at the relevant level
research_questions: Do observed lessons reuse the same examples and headings while maintaining suitable adaptation?

incremental.description: Curate example tags and template versions

approvals.approved_version: The selected lesson passage, example and intended performer group checked before instruction; live adaptations are checked before communicating them.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B100 R90 gives10 gross minus2 upkeep =8 net. Low: only a few examples match the learner level and most exercises need rewriting, leaving retrieval19, preparation14, teaching55 and notes9, R97; net1. High: examples are tagged and lesson headings fit but adaptations stay personal, leaving18+12+55+8=93 retained, minus2 upkeep gives5 net.

tasks.short: Observe and interpret movements, then write and organise the choreography record.

steps.what: Observe dance movements and identify the routine passage being recorded
Interpret technical aspects, patterns and formations for the choreography record
Record movements and technical details using the chosen choreography notation
Index the record by routine version, passage and supporting media references
Check recorded movements against the observed sequence and correct ambiguity

tasks.design: Configure notation-compatible page structures and routine metadata in {DOCS}. The choreographer observes and interprets movement, writes the technical content and checks it; templates reuse record structure rather than infer choreography from video.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring notation layouts and media references are manually reconstructed.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reusable document structures and metadata can reduce mechanical record handling.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate interpretation of movement, formation changes and artistic intent.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which technical distinctions another dancer needs to reconstruct the movement.
tasks.altitude: Keep a clearer reusable choreography record with less layout work.

evidence.claim: A notation-compatible document template can reuse layout, but this does not establish automatic dance transcription; benefit is E1.

assumptions: The task's record writing is included as s3, separately from observing and interpreting movement.
The choreographer supplies routine identity in s1, interpreted details in s2 and passage, version and media references in s4. Capture time is counted; absent metadata is entered manually.
Try the existing notation workflow and native document layouts first; unsupported notation requires manual entry.
Ordinary author saves stay included at full effort with no approval stage or claimed saving.
unknowns: Chosen notation and compatibility with native templates
Completeness of existing passage and media identifiers
research_questions: Can the native template retain the chosen notation and reduce layout effort without losing reconstruction detail?

already_counted.description: Full movement observation, interpretation and accuracy checking

incremental.description: Maintain notation templates and metadata conventions
